rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (60 development trials): raising ki 0.05 to 0.3 and kp 2.0 to 2.5 changed almost nothing. Oval progress stayed at 0.11, max_error at 0.0622 m, and line_loss_events at 1.0 in every run. s-bend and slalom moved only slightly. steering_oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.15), so the robot is not weaving. The motor-mismatch drift hypothesis (H1) is therefore not supported as the main cause. The failure is a repeatable line loss at about the same point of the course, not a slow drift that the integral could fix. The gain-independent progress and max_error point to a sensing or speed limit. The outer sensors sit at x = ±0.03 m. With a 12 mm footprint and a 12.5 mm tape half-width, they stop seeing tape at about 0.043 m offset. The off-track limit is 0.06 m, so the robot is effectively blind for the last ~17 mm before it leaves the track. Line loss then triggers the last_direction search, which does not recover. The base_speed of 1.6 is also high for the sharper bends (s-bend and slalom), so the robot arrives too fast to correct. I make two changes. (1) Widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.04 m, so tape is still visible at about 0.053 m offset and the line is detected before the off-track limit. (2) Lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.3, following the Evaluator's rule for bend-entry failures. I keep kp = 2.5, ki = 0.3 and kd = 0.1, because oscillation did not rise and the gain changes had no measurable effect. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, progress rising above 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, and max_error falling below 0.06 m. Speed will drop, so completion time may get worse, but the robot must stay on the line before speed matters. Hypotheses: (H2) line loss is caused by the sensor span being too narrow; (H3) the failure is caused by speed on bend entries. Measurements to check next: progress and line_loss_events per track, max_error, and whether the failure point moves along the course. If progress still stalls at about 0.11 with the wider span, the cause is speed, and the next step is to lower base_speed further to about 1.0.
